A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same medical interpretability study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching content across table renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original measurements and visualizations of five LLMs using UMAP, weight saliency, layer lesioning, and activation patching, with further results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical study and adds interpretability measurements for six additional medical LLMs in Tables 3, 7, and 8.

M1.justification: The four-part knowledge-mapping procedure remains unchanged. New Section 4.1 proposes training adaptations using age-linearity, embedding-uniformity, and disease-progression monotonicity losses. These are additional proposed objectives, not demonstrated changes to the evaluated models or mapping pipeline.

E1.justification: The age, symptom, disease, disease-progression, drug, and dosage tasks remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same prompt templates and four nine-stage disease trajectories. Additional evaluated LLMs expand model configurations rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Neither version introduces a competing interpretability method evaluated against the mapping approach. The six additional LLMs are subjects of the same analyses, rather than new baseline methods for evaluating the proposed procedure.

E3.justification: The evaluated model set expands substantially from five to eleven: v2 adds OpenBioLLM-70B, PMC-LLaMA-13B, ClinicalCamel-70B, PalmyraMed-70B, Meditron-70B, and HuatuoGPT-o1-70B. Tables 3, 7, and 8 apply the retained metrics at the best layer, across layers, and at the final layer. Newly disclosed UMAP settings do not establish changes to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: The disease-progression case study has revised closest-stage trajectories in Figures 4 and 15, changing the layerwise evidence concerning non-monotonicity. Other investigations, including layer lesioning and the dosage case study, are retained. The proposed regularizers receive no ablation or validation experiments.

E5.justification: Bootstrap confidence intervals, aggregation across prompts, and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting are already present in v1 and remain in v2. The additional tables follow existing reporting practices. Changed uncertainty values do not establish new estimation procedures, seeds, or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Tables 3, 7, and 8 add extensive results for six models. Disease-progression values also change throughout Tables 1 and 2 and v1 Table 5/v2 Table 6. For example, Llama's best-layer CSFS changes from 3.25 ± 0.43 at layer 11 to 6.25 ± 2.17 at layer 0; its final-layer CSLS changes from 6.50 ± 0.50 to 4.50 ± 1.66. The PDFs do not explain these revisions.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds explicit mathematical definitions for age-linearity, hyperspherical-uniformity, and monotonic-progression regularizers. These are limited formal additions without proofs or guarantees. The original silhouette, anisotropy, activation-patching, and layer-selection mathematics remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: medical knowledge maps using four techniques, nonlinear age representations, circular disease progression, drug clustering, and intermediate activation collapse. Additional model results and training recommendations do not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: New Section 4.1 develops practical implications into specific recommendations for removing age discontinuities, preventing representation collapse, and enforcing monotonic disease progression. Earlier interpretations and the lack-of-ground-truth limitation remain unchanged. The proposed remedies are not empirically validated.

D1.justification: v2 specifies UMAP n_neighbors = 15, min_dist = 0.1, and cosine distance, which v1 does not disclose. It also replaces the statement that code is attached with an explicit repository address. These improve documented reproducibility without establishing changed settings in the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang and Isola (2020) to support the uniformity-loss recommendation and removes the Dubey et al. Llama 3 reference and Llama 3 model-card entry. The related-work discussion and overall novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. v2 adds the actionable-recommendations subsection, Appendix G, and acknowledgments, with limited caption edits and updated publication headers. This is a localized structural expansion rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: The main results layout is substantially reorganized: several figures are enlarged, Figures 5–7 are grouped on one page, and Figure 8 is repositioned relative to its explanatory text. Three new result tables are added, while existing appendix tables are renumbered. Most retained appendix figures preserve their layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation and main-figure readability, while additional medical-model comparisons help assess how broadly the observed patterns apply. These are useful but limited gains. Ground-truth validation remains absent, the new regularizers are untested, and substantial disease-progression score revisions are unexplained, so a major overall improvement is not established.
